steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Nightly counts** in *Upserts and transactions*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

ON CONFLICT (station) DO UPDATE SET bikes = station_counts.bikes + excluded.bikes;

steps.explain: Mill Bridge existed with 1 bike, so the UPDATE branch ran: 1 + 4. Only `bikes` was in the SET, so `updated` kept its old value.

steps.title: Rebuild Nightly counts cold
prompt: Recount the bikes with status `ok` at every station and write the result into `station_counts` with **updated = '2026-11-12'**. Existing stations are updated; stations with no row yet are inserted. Stations with no `ok` bikes are left alone.
- `bikes(id, model, station, status, km)`: `status` defaults to `'ok'` and `km` to `0`; `station` is NULL for a bike in the depot
- `repairs(id, bike_id, reported, issue, fixed)`: `id` is assigned automatically; `fixed` defaults to `0`
- `incoming(id, model)`: new bikes delivered to the depot
- `station_counts(station, bikes, updated)`: `station` is the primary key
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
